title: Running out of Claude tokens - which way should I use to get more?
author: Sekhmet-CustosAurora
selftext:
I use Opus 5.5 Medium for my game dev work, but I find that I run out of tokens about halfway through the week if I'm consistently 'working' on it. I'm not sure which way of getting more tokens would be best:

- Making a second Claude account with another subscription and switching between them
- Upgrading to Max, which would give me plenty of tokens for Opus and I'm sure enough for some Fable use, but costs 5x as much
- Buying usage credits, which I'm assuming gives you less for your money than a subscription
- Swapping to my existing ChatGPT Plus subscription and using GPT-6.2 Astra. I mostly use ChatGPT for general questions. I'm not sure how much usage I'd get, and I don't want to run out of usage for my non-coding uses.
- Buying a Gemini subscription and trying out Gemini 4 Neon, I'm told it's pretty good for its value 
- Using a cheap and inferior model either locally or in the cloud

Which would you recommend?

comments.author: Skubcraft
comments.body: Codex has a free plan with GPT Luna. What I do is I'll make spec sheets for various tasks and send them off to Luna for implementation.

comments.author: kokutouchichi
comments.body: I use chatgpt and Claude interchangeably, no issues. Make sure you are starting new sessions for each major task. Think of how you can optimize your downtime. There are plenty of decisions you can make while the game is working on code or you are waiting for a reset. Story, dialogue, ui design.

replies.author: Sekhmet-CustosAurora
replies.body: there's basically nothing I can do with the downtime. It's something of a Minecraft clone (not really but close enough) that there isn't and won't be much story or dialogue to speak of. Assets are using a resource pack for now, will only start replacing them when it is at the point of being an actual game

comments.author: count023
comments.body: you should be offloading all coding work to sonnet and all simple query work to Haiku, opus should not be doing everything and doesnt need to. have opus do your planning, have sonnet do your coding, and have haiku do your data collection (like pulling stats for units together or esearching sources onlline). That'll stretch you out a lot more than you realize. gemini has a free cli tier as well, but it's quite limited, and is usefl for offloading osme tasks is it's just a 5 hour rolling reset that has no weekly limit, just hte 5 hour cooldown.

replies.author: DaedalusRaistlin
replies.body:
If you're using the Claude desktop app in Code mode, you can get it to propose a new session. If shows a session card and the Options button let's you select which model implements it. The session is handed enough detail to begin work immediately (it's good at passing information between sessions, even later on.)

It's not really automated, just easier. The model doesn't seem to be able to pick itself or switch on its own. 

Using Claude Code in VS Code doesn't do this in my experience, but you can ask Claude to give you a prompt to paste into a new conversation, and set which model to use before you send the message. I don't think it's a good idea to change the model mid session, you have to use a new chat session, otherwise the new model will read everything the prior model did. 

It's still a bit cumbersome, but it works.

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
Just implement a rule; sonnet does coding and opus only checks and planning. No need for anything else. 
Don't forget you also can ask for tests without context which is really helpful if you want a more neutral view.

comments.author: jimbojohndoe
comments.body:
So I got max account on Claude, GPT pro account, and an ultra Google plan, currently so may not be super applicable unless you are at the highest tier. 

I personally would say though, go use Gemini Neon and Carbon if you are looking for another account.

Gemini Neon is a rock star fine-tuning the optimization requests and creative decision making I had asked Claude Fable 5.2 to do prior, which Fable great but it still took Fable awhile to do them. 

I still like GPT the most for creatively changing environments and such, but Neon does a good enough job that I been hashing it out for a couple days creatively, and quite satisfied.

I can't say too much about usage as I only started using Gemini this week after maxing Claude and GPT this week, but in two days it was 10% usage for the weekly usage with Neon, which was for one game. Most were enhancement requests and optimizations on my existing Godot 3d game.  
After 3 days, its 62% since I started using Carbon on High, so for like 5 small games, 1 large 3d game, and 3d modeling.

comments.author: delicious_pubes
comments.body:
Do not buy usage credits until you are already using ultra tier usage. 

I pay $200 a month because I’m bougie like that and have more fun sending off fable and opus to do everything but there are some easy ways to mitigate token waste if you aren’t already doing them: clear your conversations after each big task and if you want to continue work, ask it for a prompt to give a fresh convo. This is much more efficient than compaction. 

Also ask it where it is using tokens and where you could save in your workflow, as a project scales you need to do periodic check ins on token waste and overall architecture to make sure it is efficient for the agent

comments.author: RemarkableWish2508
comments.body:
> Buying usage credits, which I'm assuming gives you less for your money than a subscription

Risky assumption. Subscriptions include multiple features, wouldn't be the first time when someone sells a printer with a "sample" amount of ink bundled with it. Better double check how much you get with which... every time (since subscriptions don't list the exact amount of tokens).

Using a cheaper model for less demanding parts of the whole work, is definitely a good idea. Right now, Gemini tokens are a couple to several times cheaper than Claude ones for a similar effectivity (may change without warning).

comments.author: dnr424
comments.body: You should keep global instructions short and split project docs into smaller files based on functionality. Use short summaries and directory-level AGENTS.md files so the agent only loads what it needs for the current task. This helps cut down unnecessary token burn.
